summary: This prologue introduces the Sirah Impak Sosial series. The ustaz explains why this series is different: the sirah is read together with the state of the community today, and every session ends with action. Its title is 'The Weariness of the Ummah, the Light at the End of the Tunnel', and to show why the sirah matters he begins not with the Prophet's ﷺ birth but three months before his death: the Farewell Hajj and the Farewell Sermon before 124,000 pilgrims. Those last messages, from the sanctity of blood and property, the abolition of usury and women's rights to there being no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, are compared with our condition. He lists the problems the series aims to answer: shallow religiosity, material obsession, loneliness and extreme heedlessness, then shows how the Prophet's ﷺ character answers them all. The ustaz closes with the hadith of the Prophet's ﷺ longed-for brothers, and a Q&A on the Prophetic Strategy Summit in Istanbul and parenting.
keyPoints: The series reads the sirah together with the reality of the community today, and each session ends with awareness and action, not just a story.

The Farewell Sermon before 124,000 pilgrims affirmed the sanctity of blood, property and honour, the abolition of usury, mindfulness of Allah in dealing with women, and no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab. The ustaz asks how far that message is carried out.
After the sermon the Prophet ﷺ asked those present to pass it on to those absent, and now that 'baton' is in our hands.
Age and physical ability are not limits: the example of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari RA, who fought until almost 90 years old, and the Companions had no concept of retirement.
The problems the sirah is to answer: shallow religiosity, material obsession, loneliness and extreme heedlessness, and a lifestyle without the Prophet's ﷺ guidance.

Change begins with a small group (around 3 percent) and from our sphere of influence: spouse, children, neighbours. The hadith of the Prophet's ﷺ brothers reminds us of our responsibility to follow him.

people.context: The previous session finished the story of Prophet Adam AS. About 124,000 prophets were sent and all of us are written to be the community of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Sent by the Prophet ﷺ to lead the pilgrims a year before the Farewell Hajj.
The Prophet ﷺ told him, as he sent him off, that this might be the last time they met and he would only see the Prophet's ﷺ mosque and grave.
The first usury the Prophet ﷺ abolished in the Farewell Sermon was his own.

people.role: Companion, host of the Prophet ﷺ at the Hijra
people.context: Joined the army at nearly 90 for the sake of the hadith on the opening of Constantinople, and was buried as close as possible to that city's walls.
The story of his people who stuffed their ears illustrates the wall of ghaflah.
Shows the Prophet ﷺ relaxing: racing and watching a show, not always tense.
Was present when the Bedouin urinated in the mosque and the Prophet ﷺ asked for water to wash it, rather than hitting him.
At Badr asked for retaliation because he had been poked by the Prophet's ﷺ stick while straightening the rows, then kissed his belly because he wanted to be the last person he touched.

lessons.title: The baton of the Prophet's ﷺ message is now in our hands
lessons.body: The message 'convey it to those who are absent' was carried on by the Companions until today. The series is designed so that we do not just listen to stories.

lessons.title: Age and physical ability are no excuse
lessons.body: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari fought at almost 90. The ustaz also mentions a person in a wheelchair who inspired thousands of young people.

lessons.title: The Companions had no concept of retirement
lessons.body: They crossed the desert with little provision to maximise effort and hope for Allah's reward, even though Paradise was already assured to them.

lessons.title: The sirah is a 'litmus' test to recognise our problems
lessons.body: When we see how the Prophet ﷺ taught and how we live differently, only then do we realise we may be part of the problem without knowing.

lessons.title: Whatever our problems, they are in the Prophet's ﷺ life
lessons.body: Losing family members, exile, poverty. That is why the sirah can be connected with our lives today.

lessons.title: The sirah is not a disconnected story from 1,500 years ago
lessons.body: Young people often find it hard to connect with. Every inch of the sirah can be connected if the process of drawing lessons is done properly, and the result must be action.

lessons.title: Change begins with a small group of around 3 percent
lessons.body: Of 124,000 Companions, only around 300 are recorded. The ustaz mentions a formula that at least 3 percent of a society acting can change society.

lessons.title: Answer young people's questions, don't knock their heads
lessons.body: Many teenagers feel nothing about religion and ask why be a Muslim. The question must be answered so it does not turn into resentment of the religion.

lessons.title: Look at the essence, not the label or the clothes
lessons.body: Abu Jahl also wore a robe and turban. What makes the difference is character, belief and way of life, and an institution named Islam does not guarantee the essence.

lessons.title: The sirah is the closest door to knowing the Prophet ﷺ
lessons.body: Through the course of his life the heart will feel he is truly the Messenger of Allah, and his character was what first drew people's hearts at that time.

lessons.title: Give full attention, not multitasking
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ turned his full attention to the one speaking, and even put down a ring he was fiddling with because it disturbed his focus.

lessons.title: Entertainment is allowed, but not to excess
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ allowed Ansari girls to sing on the festival day, raced with Aisha and watched a show. What is worrying is nonstop entertainment until deep thinking is lost.

lessons.title: Handle difficult people with wisdom
lessons.body: When the Bedouin urinated in the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ held back the Companions, advised him gently and had it washed. It touches the heart of difficult people.

lessons.title: Focus on our sphere of influence
lessons.body: Don't be busy with too many worrying things. Put effort into your spouse, children, neighbours and roles you have, and measure progress, not just 'doing'.

lessons.title: Prophetic parenting: loved, trusted, then religion
lessons.body: Before teaching prayer, a child must feel most loved and then most trusting so that they have a safe space. The ustaz reminds us not to skip those two steps.

glossary.meaning: The ustaz's method: learning the sirah together with the state of the community and ending each session with action.
The community's weakness as the Prophet ﷺ explained it: love of the world and fear of death.
The farewell Hajj, the Prophet's ﷺ only Hajj, three months before his death.
The Prophet's ﷺ last sermon at Arafah that summed up the main teachings.
Heedlessness, especially extreme heedlessness such that one cannot listen or think deeply.
A term the ustaz mentions from the national health survey, referring to teenage depression linked to the digital world.
The range of things we can directly influence, as distinct from the wider 'circle of concern'.
Believers who have not met the Prophet ﷺ but follow him. He longs for them and distinguishes them from the Companions.
Where the Prophet ﷺ waits for his community on the Day of Judgement. Whoever drinks from his hand will never thirst again.
The approach to parenting following the Prophet ﷺ, starting with love and trust before teaching religion.

dalil.context: The ustaz uses it to explain the weariness of the ummah. The Companions asked what wahn is and the Prophet ﷺ explained it.
dalil.translation: The nations will be summoned against the community like diners to a dish; their numbers will be many but they will be like foam on the sea, struck by the disease of wahn, which is love of the world and fear of death.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ asked which day, land and month this was to draw attention, then replied that blood, property and honour are equally sacred. This is the first principle he stressed.
dalil.translation: Indeed your blood and your property are sacred to you, as sacred as this day, in this month, in this land. Everything of the Jahiliyyah is abolished beneath my feet.

dalil.context: The ustaz asks how our economy, which today stands on usury, fares.
dalil.translation: The usury of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first usury the Prophet ﷺ abolished was the usury of Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib.

dalil.context: The ustaz asks whether women today are treated with mindfulness of Allah.
dalil.translation: Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them by Allah's trust and made their honour lawful to you by the word of Allah.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Prophet ﷺ demolished racism, gender domination and tribal nationalism, and links it to the crisis of leadership.
dalil.translation: There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab, except by taqwa.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to our responsibility to carry on that message, with the baton now in our hands.
dalil.translation: Each message was closed with the question 'have I conveyed it?', they answered yes, then the Prophet ﷺ pointed to the sky and said 'O Allah, bear witness'. Those present were asked to convey it to those absent.

dalil.context: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari RA heard this message and joined the army at almost 90 years old and was buried beside that city's walls.
dalil.translation: Constantinople will be conquered. The best army is its army, and the best commander is its commander.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Prophet ﷺ lost his father, mother, uncle and wife, buried six of his seven children himself, was exiled and poor, so whatever problems we have are in the sirah.
dalil.translation: The people most severely tested are the prophets, then those like them, and so on.

dalil.context: Allah made the Quran easy to remember. The ustaz says it is not so easy in experience, so the sirah becomes a closer door. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We have made it easy to learn lessons from the Quran: will anyone take heed?

dalil.context: The ustaz says the main theme of this surah is the remedy for material obsession.
dalil.translation: Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday, it will be a light for him until the next Friday.

dalil.context: Be patient with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, and do not turn your eyes from them desiring worldly adornment. The ustaz links it to brotherhood and the remedy for material obsession. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Content yourself with those who pray to their Lord morning and evening, seeking His approval, and do not let your eyes turn away from them out of desire for the attractions of this worldly life: do not yield to those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our Quran, those who follow their own low desires, those whose ways are unbridled.

dalil.context: The people of Prophet Nuh put their fingers in their ears so as not to hear. The ustaz likens it to the wall of ghaflah and the mental space that has no room to hear good. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: every time I call them, so that You may forgive them, they thrust their fingers into their ears, cover their heads with their garments, persist in their rejection, and grow more insolent and arrogant.

dalil.context: Mentioned by the ustaz in the lifestyle section, along with the advice to sleep early after Isha if there is nothing important to do.
dalil.translation: The stomach is divided into three: food, water and breath. Eat only enough to keep the back straight.

dalil.context: The ustaz warns us not to misunderstand the sirah and then say 'the Prophet did this'.
dalil.translation: Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.

dalil.context: The Companions asked 'aren't we your brothers?' and he replied that they were Companions, while the brothers would come later.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ visited the graveyard, greeted its dwellers, then said he longed to meet his brothers, the believers who are not yet born. He will recognise them by the light of their ablution marks and wait at the basin, but some will be driven away for changing the teaching.

dalil.context: Say, if you truly love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you. The ustaz stresses there is only one way to Allah's love, the way of the Prophet ﷺ. Surah Ali Imran is mentioned, the verse number is not. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Say, ‘If you love God, follow me, and God will love you and forgive you your sins; God is most forgiving, most merciful.’

events.label: Dhul-Hijjah, 10 AH
events.title: The Farewell Hajj with 124,000 pilgrims
events.desc: The Prophet's ﷺ only Hajj. A year earlier Abu Bakr had led the pilgrims. He entered ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah and headed for Arafah.

events.label: Arafah
events.title: The Farewell Sermon
events.desc: The last address, without a loudspeaker, passed along in a chain to the people at the back.

events.label: Three months later
events.title: The Prophet ﷺ falls ill and dies
events.desc: The ustaz asks why we begin this story with the final event.

events.label: The Prophet's Mosque
events.title: A Bedouin urinates in the mosque
events.desc: The Prophet ﷺ stopped the Companions from acting, advised him gently, then had it washed. The Bedouin later prayed.

events.label: After the Conquest of Mecca
events.title: A youth who mocked the adhan is asked to call it again
events.desc: The Prophet ﷺ taught him the adhan properly. His descendants later became muezzins in Mecca.

events.label: Battle of Badr
events.title: Sawad ibn Ghaziyyah asks for retaliation and kisses the Prophet's ﷺ belly
events.desc: Illustrates how tense the atmosphere at Badr was, which is often memorised as just numbers of soldiers.
